newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia bourse sees steady turnover in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia bourse sees steady turnover in 1997.

text.p: The Ljubljana Stock Exchange said on Thursday a lack of transparent foreign investment laws and new taxes on trading profits were likely to keep trading volumes on the seven-year old bourse at this year's level.

Overall turnover, including shares, bonds and short-term securities on the main and the over-the-counter (OTC) markets, is expected to exceed 80 billion tolars ($571 million) this year, little changed from 81.9 billion tolars in 1995.

"We hope a new take-over law and a new law on cross-border financial transactions will be introduced next year, because the absence of such laws is an obstacle to our development," bourse chief Drasko Veselinovic told a news conference.

"There is a lot of foreign interest, but it is impeded by unclear legislation," he added. Currently, foreigners have to register every transaction on the Slovenian market with the country's central bank.
The bourse also said a new 25 percent tax on trading profits, which individual investors will have to pay from January, will mean a further obstacle to the development of Slovenia's fledgling bourse.
The tax is already applied to institutional investors' trading profits.
Veselinovic said the market could expect some 30 listings of newly privatised companies on the main and OTC markets in 1997, up from 27 new listings this year.
The main market's total capitalisation rose to 91.5 billion tolars ($654.8 million) on November 29, up from 38.6 billion tolars at the end of 1995.
Currently, 25 shares are traded on the main market and another 27 on the OTC market.
